facts.statement: The small-billed moa-nalo was an extinct, flightless, goose-like duck.
facts.quote: The small-billed moa-nalo (Ptaiochen pau), also known as the stumbling moa-nalo, is a species of moa-nalo, one of a group of extinct, flightless, large goose-like ducks

facts.statement: The species was described in 1991 by Storrs Olson and Helen James based on material collected in September 1982.
facts.quote: It was described in 1991 from subfossil material collected in September 1982 by Storrs Olson, Helen James and others

facts.statement: Fossils were found at Auwahi Cave on the southern slopes of Haleakalā on the island of Maui.
facts.quote: from the Auwahi Cave on the southern slopes of Haleakalā, on the island of Maui

facts.statement: Like the genus Thambetochen, this species had bony, tooth-like projections on its jaws.
facts.quote: The species was similar to moa-nalo in the genus Thambetochen in having bony, tooth-like projections on the jaws

facts.statement: It had a proportionately shorter and deeper rostrum compared to other moa-nalo.
facts.quote: it differed in other aspects of skull morphology, such as in having a proportionately shorter and deeper rostrum

facts.statement: The skull featured a more rounded cranium and lacked impressions of salt glands.
facts.quote: a more rounded cranium, and in lacking impressions of salt-glands

facts.statement: Remains were found exclusively at altitudes above 1100 meters on Haleakalā.
facts.quote: Subfossil remains have been found only at altitudes of over 1100 m on Haleakalā

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered ranging from 1145 meters at Auwahi Cave to 1860 meters in the upper Kipahulu Valley.
facts.quote: from the Auwahi Cave at 1145 m to the upper Kipahulu Valley at 1860 m
